name: PT Global Digital Niaga Tbk

frontmatter.title: Blibli: growth bought with margin, and a price that still pays for it
frontmatter.summary: We initiate Blibli at REDUCE with a Rp188 target, -19.2% from the Rp232 price. The 46.0% revenue growth is institution and store volume at a 15.6% gross margin, not marketplace compounding. Our DCF is Rp72 and the price is 3.28 times fundamental value. One input is unresolved: the free float (governance section).
thesis: The growth is a mix story, not a moat story: institution revenue rose 70.0% and physical stores 37.0% while the third-party marketplace grew 9.0%, so gross margin fell to 15.6% from 17.6% [S3][S7].
The equity story is the cost line: operating expense moved -1.0% year on year while revenue rose 46.0%, and our base turns EBIT positive in FY2028E at IDR607.6bn [S3].
DCF value is Rp72 and the EV/sales cross-check Rp78; blended value today is Rp73 and the twelve-month fundamental value Rp80.
At Rp232 the shares sit at 3.28 times fundamental value; the konglo lens keeps most of that premium, so the target is Rp188, a -19.2% return.

Funding is the tail risk: net debt reaches IDR7,720.1bn at its peak in FY2029E, near book equity, and a placement of up to 9.5bn shares was proposed to the June 2026 meetings but is not approved or priced in our sources [S8].

catalysts.event: High-shareholding-concentration shares, Blibli included, leave the IHSG calculation
FY2026 audited accounts due, the first full-year print on the post-efficiency cost base
First step of the exchange's free-float staircase if the company's float is below the lowest tier
MSCI decision on Indonesia Standalone status, the cohort-wide regime event

blocks.text: *Revision note.* The quality check's first pass found the D&A line set on the data pack rather than on the company's own nine-month bridge. This version restates D&A to the reported basis, re-cuts capex and the borrowing path with it, and corrects the valuation bridge, the konglo compression wording, the post- balance-sheet record and the ownership reconciliation. The rating is unchanged.

We initiate PT Global Digital Niaga (BELI) at **REDUCE** with a twelve-month target of Rp188, -19.2% against the Rp232 last price. That target is not a fundamental-value call alone: the fundamental twelve-month value is Rp80, the shares trade at 3.28 times today's scenario-weighted value of 70.78, and the konglo overlay keeps only part of that premium over the next year. The call is that the market is still paying for a quality of growth the accounts do not show. One input is flagged rather than resolved: the two ownership sources disagree on the free float, and the governance section states both figures and what each would do to the overlay.

The operating record is genuinely better than it was. Net revenue for the first nine months of 2026 was IDR22.24tn, up 46.0%, the operating loss halved to IDR-0.78tn and the EBITDA loss fell 61.0% to IDR-0.57tn while operating expense moved -1.0% year on year to IDR4.31tn [S2][S3]. Management frames this as quality growth and capital discipline, and on the cost side it is [S2].

What the mix says is different. The fastest-growing lines are the lowest-margin ones: institution revenue rose 70.0% to IDR9.92tn and physical-store revenue 37.0% to IDR6.63tn, against 9.0% growth in the third-party marketplace at IDR1.20tn [S3]. Gross margin fell to 15.6% from 17.6%, and the company attributes it to the change in product and revenue mix [S7]. Transaction value grew 11.0% to IDR67.17tn while revenue grew 46.0%, which is the arithmetic signature of low-take-rate distribution volume rather than marketplace compounding [S3].

Three things move the value. First, the operating-expense path: our base carries the ratio from 18.7% of revenue in FY2026E to 11.2% in FY2030E, which is the single largest lever in the model and the one the last two prints support [S3][S6]. Second, the gross margin, where mix has been running against the company; we hold it near the current level rather than assume a recovery [S3]. Third, funding: the group has funded this company with fresh equity as well as debt — the share count rose from 118,493m at the IPO to 135,843m in FY2025A, and gross debt has risen every year since — and the placement proposed in May is the next test of how that is done [S0][S8].

Valuation is set out in the valuation section: a DCF at Rp72 carrying most of the weight, an EV/sales cross-check at Rp78 carrying the rest, a cost of capital inside the house band for rupiah cash flows, and a konglo overlay that recognises the price may not converge to value within a year. The overlay is why the rating is REDUCE rather than SELL.

Blibli is the Djarum group's consumer-internet and retail vehicle. PT Global Digital Niaga Tbk operates the Blibli marketplace, the tiket.com online travel agency, the Ranch Market supermarket chain and the Dekoruma home and living business, and describes itself as an integrated omnichannel commerce and lifestyle ecosystem [S2][S6]. The data pack records its address in Kudus, Central Java and its largest shareholder as PT Global Investama Andalan, the family holding vehicle through which the Hartono family controls the group's listed assets [S0][S9].

The company reports four revenue segments. In the first nine months of 2026 institution revenue was IDR9.92tn (+70.0%), physical stores IDR6.63tn (+37.0%), first-party retail IDR4.50tn (+29.0%) and third-party marketplace and OTA IDR1.20tn (+9.0%), for consolidated net revenue of IDR22.24tn [S2][S3]. Group gross profit before discount rose 20.0% to IDR6.11tn while reported gross profit rose 29.0% to IDR3.46tn, so discounts grew more slowly than underlying product profit: the margin fell because the fastest-growing revenue lines are the lowest-margin ones, not because discounting worsened [S3][S7]. The company says the first-party business has shifted its focus to higher-margin products while the institution and store formats scale fastest, and the disclosure shows the marketplace line growing far more slowly than the distribution lines [S2][S3]. Physical stores are the consumer-electronics chain, and the institution segment is business and public-sector distribution [S2][S3].

Operating scale is real. Total processing value was IDR67.17tn in the first nine months, up 11.0%, across 4.5m transacting users [S3]; the group ran 347 consumer-electronics stores at the end of September 2026 against 265 at the end of 2025, plus Ranch Market supermarkets and Dekoruma home centres, and it distributes through 15 warehouses and a hub network with two-hour delivery in more than forty cities [S2][S6]. The take rate on that volume rose to 9.1% [S2].

The strategy management states is "scale what works": drive transaction volume, improve margin, monetise the platform, hold the cost base and deepen customer loyalty across the ecosystem, with data analytics and AI applied to merchandising and product discovery [S2][S6]. The claim we test in the financial section is whether that programme is funded by marketplace economics or by distribution volume bought with working capital.

Blibli is a challenger, not the leader. The Indonesian e-commerce market is dominated by players several times its transaction value, and the company's own disclosure shows the marketplace line growing at single digits while the distribution lines grow far faster than the marketplace [S3].

The Indonesian e-commerce market has consolidated around a small number of platforms with national
logistics, payments and a captive ecosystem of digital services. Scale in that market comes from
frequency and fulfilment density, and the firms that lost share usually did so on logistics cost per order
rather than on assortment. Blibli's omnichannel push, including the physical electronics chain and the
premium supermarket format, is a bid to raise frequency and basket size without paying online acquisition
cost for every order.

The measured market is still growing at a double-digit rate, but not at the rate Blibli's revenue implies. Indonesia's digital economy reached 119bn of gross merchandise value in 2026, up 16.0%, of which e-commerce was 85bn, also up 16.0%, according to the e-Conomy SEA 2026 report by Google, Temasek and Bain [S10]. The same report projects the digital economy at 446bn or more by 2035, which supports a long runway for the category but says nothing about which platform captures it [S10].

Against that market, Blibli's transaction value of IDR67.17tn for nine months is roughly a mid-single-digit share of annual e-commerce value, and its revenue grows faster than the market only because institution and store revenue are consolidated gross while marketplace GMV is not [S3][S10]. That distinction matters for any cross-check based on sales: the company's revenue line is not comparable with a pure marketplace's take rate.

Competitive position is weakest exactly where the margin is. The marketplace grew 9.0% in the first nine months while first-party grew 29.0% on a stated shift to higher-margin products [S3][S2]. That is a rational margin decision inside the company, but it concedes that the platform does not win on assortment breadth against larger rivals. The physical chain and the premium supermarket format are the differentiated assets: they give Blibli owned demand, supplier terms and a fulfilment network that a pure marketplace cannot replicate quickly, and management is explicit that store expansion is central to the omnichannel strategy [S2][S6].

Five forces, briefly. Supplier power is moderate and falling for consumer electronics, where the group's store count gives it buying scale, but weak in grocery, where suppliers price nationally [S2]. Buyer power is high: Indonesian shoppers switch platforms for vouchers, and the company's own discount line is material in the segment disclosure [S5]. New entrants are constrained by logistics and capital, but the incumbent rivals are not new entrants — they are larger platforms with deeper pockets [S10]. Substitutes are the traditional retail channels the company is itself buying into. Rivalry is the dominant force, and it is why a 46.0% revenue increase came with a falling gross margin [S7].

Regulation now matters to the share price as much as to the business. The exchange has been tightening disclosure and index treatment of high-shareholding-concentration companies, and from 13 November 2026 those shares leave the IHSG calculation [S12]. The house registry records Blibli on that list, with a reported free float of 23.8% [S13]. MSCI has proposed Standalone status for Indonesia, with a decision due by the end of June 2027, which is a cohort-wide event rather than a Blibli-specific one [S13].

The demand backdrop is not supportive. Our house macro regime is cautious, with an avoid tilt on Indonesian consumer discretionary, and the macro deck carries the rupiah at 18,350 against a spot near 17,968 with the policy rate at 5.8: a weaker currency raises the landed cost of the imported electronics that anchor the store and first-party lines and compresses the real disposable income that funds discretionary baskets [S0]. Blibli earns and spends in rupiah, so the effect is through demand and input cost rather than translation.

The moat test is the one the compounder card demands, and Blibli does not pass it yet. There are switching costs inside the ecosystem — the co-branded card, the loyalty programme, the travel and grocery adjacencies — but there is no evidence they are widening: transacting users grew 10.0% against 11.0% transaction-value growth, which is more users at the same spend rather than deeper engagement [S3]. Distribution density is real (15 warehouses, a hub network, two-hour delivery) but it is being built with capital the business does not yet generate [S2][S3].

The five-year record is one of a company that grew revenue while losing money, and only recently began to lose less of it. Revenue went from IDR15,269.1bn in FY2022A to IDR22,361.0bn in FY2025A, gross margin from 8.0% to 17.5%, and the operating result from IDR-5,007.2bn to IDR-1,987.8bn [S0]. Free cash flow was negative every year, at IDR-3,800.9bn in FY2025A, because the operating loss plus working capital absorbed more than depreciation provided [S0].

The 2026 prints change the slope. Nine-month revenue was IDR22.24tn and gross profit IDR3.46tn, with the gross margin at 15.6% [S2][S7]. Operating expense fell to IDR4.31tn, against 26.6% of revenue in FY2025A [S3][S6]. That is the whole improvement: gross profit grew 29.0% and the cost base did not grow at all [S7].

Our forecast extends exactly that arithmetic rather than assuming a second, larger efficiency programme. FY2026E is the nine-month actual of IDR22.24tn plus a fourth quarter grown at the third quarter's rate, which gives IDR31,529.1bn and growth of 41.0%; the earlier number implied a fourth-quarter step-down that no source supports [S2][S6]. Revenue then grows 22.0%, 17.0% and 14.0%, converging on the measured market rate as the institution segment annualises [S10]. Gross margin holds at 15.6% and recovers only to 16.5% by FY2030E as the take rate rises and new stores mature [S2]. Operating expense is modelled as an absolute line — the nine-month cost base of IDR4.31tn annualised and grown with the store estate and inflation — so the ratio falls from 18.7% of revenue to 11.2% because revenue grows, not because a second efficiency programme is assumed [S3][S6].

One line has to be restated before the forecast can be read. The data pack's D&A is roughly double the charge the company's own nine-month bridge implies: the reported EBITDA of IDR-0.57tn against an operating loss of IDR-0.78tn gives D&A of 1.0% of revenue, and the same arithmetic on the prior-year comparative gives the same answer [S3]. The pack's 9M26 EBITDA is correspondingly higher than the company's — the two EBIT figures agree, only the add-back differs — so the pack carries an inflated depreciation line [S0][S3]. We model the company basis, 1.0% of revenue. Capex was re-cut with that line so terminal reinvestment still equals g/ROIC — capex converges on the depreciation charge plus the growth investment rather than carrying the old ratio that was tied to the pack's D&A [S0][S3]. The pack's FY2025A history is left as the pack reports it; comparisons between our FY2026E and the pack's FY2025A should be made on margins, not levels.

The resulting path is: EBIT of IDR-977.4bn in FY2026E, positive in FY2028E at IDR607.6bn, and IDR3,028.2bn by FY2030E, a 5.3% operating margin [S0]. EBITDA loss narrows to IDR-662.1bn in FY2026E — a -2.1% margin, consistent with the nine-month print — and turns positive a year later only just, at IDR76.9bn, which is the number to watch against management's own framing of the path to profitability [S2][S3]. Net profit is still marginally negative in FY2028E, at IDR-60.4bn, because interest on the funding gap runs ahead of the operating recovery, and the first positive year is FY2029E at IDR732.4bn [S0].

Cash is the constraint. Free cash flow improves from IDR-3,800.9bn to IDR-1,404.0bn in FY2026E and turns positive in FY2029E at IDR145.9bn, but the cumulative gap has to be funded [S0]. We assume new borrowing of IDR900.0bn in FY2026E, rising through FY2027E as the loss persists, so that net debt peaks at IDR7,720.1bn in FY2029E, about 3.3 times that year's EBITDA and close to the book equity of the business [S0]. That is financeable for a group of this size, but it is not comfortable, and it is why the placement proposed in May matters [S8]. The model runs the debt-funded branch, because the placement has no approval, price or use of proceeds in our sources; the report prices the placement branch against it in the valuation section [S8].

Capital allocation has been equity-funded expansion. The share count rose from 118,493m in FY2022A to 135,843m in FY2025A and 137,201m in the first nine months of 2026, and no dividend has ever been paid [S0][S6]. A placement and employee scheme of up to 9.5bn shares was put to the June 2026 shareholder meetings, split between the employee programme and a general capital increase without pre-emptive rights; it is a proposal in our sources, not an approved or priced issue [S8]. The two branches matter and are priced in the valuation section: executed at the last price those shares would raise about 9.5bn times Rp232, which would retire part of the funding gap, while executed at a discount they would be issued below fundamental value and transfer value to the subscriber [S8][S0].

Earnings quality, run through the house screen. The accruals ratio is not meaningful on a loss-maker, but the direction is: FY2025A net loss of IDR-2,301.9bn against free cash flow of IDR-3,800.9bn shows a loss that consumes cash rather than an accounting charge [S0]. Two divergence flags are present and worth naming. Receivables grew faster than revenue in FY2025A, which is consistent with the institution business's payment terms and needs watching as that segment grows [S0]. Inventory also outgrew cost of sales, the signature of a first-party and store model building stock ahead of demand [S0]. Neither is manipulation-class; both are the optics of a business mix that consumes working capital.

On the regime screens we can evidence, the company sits on the exchange's concentration list (see the governance section), which is a disclosure status rather than a finding of wrongdoing [S13]. The related-party exposure we can quantify is the sale of the Halodoc stake to the parent, Global Investama Andalan, for IDR0.54tn, a related-party asset sale the company says was booked into profit — "hasil dari divestasi itu dimasukkan dalam keuntungan perusahaan" — and is now behind it [S9].

We value Blibli on a discounted cash flow as the primary method, with EV/sales as a cross-check, which is the house method set for internet platforms and the right one here: the company has no meaningful earnings multiple today, its value depends on a margin path rather than on a current cash flow, and sales are the only line the market can anchor on while the margin is being built [S0]. The weights are 80% DCF and 20% EV/sales.

The discount rate is the engine's rupiah build: a risk-free rate of 7.4%, less the sovereign default spread of 1.6%, plus a levered beta of 1.10 on a mature equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%, giving a cost of equity of 13.2% and a WACC of 12.5% at a 11.7% debt weight [S0]. The beta starts from a company parameter of 1.00 — the market beta, not the global internet default — because all of Blibli's revenue is rupiah retail and distribution, and the country and small-float risks are already priced in the country risk premium and the liquidity discount rather than in a second premium on the discount rate [S0]. That puts the WACC inside the house band for rupiah cash flows, and the sensitivity grid holds the whole band: across it the DCF moves within the range printed in the table, the blend moves with it, and the rating is REDUCE at either edge because even the bottom of the band leaves the shares far above value [S0]. The earlier draft's above-band rate raised the discount for losses the cash flows already contain, which double-counts them.

The multiple-survival test, done like-for-like. At the terminal date the business is worth the terminal block on FY2035E EBITDA of IDR4,383.4bn: a mid-single-digit multiple, well below the 37.1x the market pays today for FY2028E EBITDA of IDR1,057.6bn — the exit is cheaper than the entry, not dearer. On gross profit the DCF is internally consistent: the DCF's enterprise value of IDR11,730.8bn against FY2026E gross profit of IDR4,918.5bn today, and the terminal block against FY2035E gross profit of IDR11,535.3bn, are close multiples, with the gross profit more than twice as large at exit. A rational buyer at the terminal date pays a distributor multiple for a business with a 6.3% EBITDA margin growing at 4.0%. That is what the terminal value assumes, and it is not multiple expansion wearing a DCF costume.

The DCF gives Rp72 a share from an enterprise value of IDR11,730.8bn. The bridge to equity deducts the net debt and the minorities carried on the 30 September 2026 balance sheet and then adds the investment portfolio on that balance sheet, which the engine values at its pack carrying value [S0]. The portfolio is added, not deducted: it is an asset outside the operating business, and at roughly a tenth of the per-share value it is not a rounding item. On that arithmetic the equity value is the enterprise value less net debt and minorities plus the portfolio, and the result is the per-share value above [S0]. The EV/sales cross-check gives Rp78 at 0.43 times sales, 7.9% against the primary.

The explicit forecast runs five years at the scaled inputs and then hands off to terminal growth from FY2031E, so revenue growth steps from the FY2030E rate to 4.0% at that boundary. That step is a construction of the template rather than a forecast that growth collapses in FY2031E; the growth sensitivity in the table below is the honest range around it, and no cell in it changes the rating.

Where that multiple comes from matters, and we describe it plainly. It is the median of the covered names whose data packs carry an EV/sales — EMTK in media, MCAS in payments and telco, NFCX in IT services and WIFI in fiber and towers — each multiple shown in the peer table [S0]. It contains no marketplace. BUKA and GOTO are covered but absent from the EV/sales column for a reason: both carry net cash large enough that enterprise value is not meaningful against revenue, so the multiple is not computed for them, and GOTO's revenue is a take-rate line rather than a gross sales line anyway [S0]. Applying a median drawn from media, payments, IT services and towers to a revenue line that is mostly consolidated first-party and institution distribution sales at a 15.6% gross margin is a weak anchor, and that is why the weight is a fifth rather than the two fifths in the industry template [S0][S3]. We show the sensitivity rather than hide it: at zero weight the blend is the DCF itself, the target moves by less than the liquidity discount, and the rating does not change [S0].

Blended value today is Rp73; rolled forward at the cost of equity it is Rp83, probability-weighted across the business scenarios Rp89, and after the liquidity discount of 10.0% the twelve-month fundamental value is Rp80 [S0]. The liquidity discount is not a rounding error: the stock trades IDR782.6m a day, which is small for a company of this market value and a real cost for any position of size [S0].

What today's price implies. At Rp232 the market capitalisation is IDR31,834.8bn, or about 3.28 times the scenario-weighted fundamental value of 70.78 per share [S0]. Held against our DCF, the price sits outside the sensitivity grid altogether: in the growth-and-margin table that follows, the most favourable cell — the top corner, where revenue growth is four points higher every year and gross margin two points higher — still values the shares below today's price. The engine's reverse DCF, which solves for the revenue growth the price implies, reports that it cannot bracket the price for the same reason: no growth rate in the tested range produces it. The price therefore requires a terminal operating margin above what the mix supports, or a premium that does not converge to the operating business within the horizon — and on this float, with the index bid gone, the second is the better description [S0][S13].

The konglo lens then asks the twelve-month question separately from the business. Blibli is a Djarum-group vehicle on the exchange's concentration list, with a reported free float of 23.8% and no passive index buyer left after the IHSG exit [S13][S12]. The lens measures the price at 3.28 times fundamental value, a log premium of 1.19, and keeps part of it for twelve months: the base regime applies the deck's 35.0% base compression and then the HSC adjustment shown in the flag list, which the engine applies once — the adjusted closure is the figure in the konglo table, not the two added a second time — and the base case targets Rp173 against a fundamental value of Rp80 [S13]. The regime bear closes more of the gap and targets Rp108; the regime bull lets the premium re-expand and targets Rp296. Probability-weighted against the business scenarios, the target is Rp188. The overlay carries no free-float deadline adjustment because the registry records the company above the floor; if the data pack's insider figure is the true measure, that adjustment applies and the target falls, as the governance section sets out [S13][S0].

Why that is the most likely path for this name rather than a cautious one: the forced index selling is done, but nothing in the ownership structure creates a buyer — the controller does not need to buy, the reported float is small, and the group's capital-markets agenda runs the other way, with a placement mandate proposed to shareholders [S8][S13]. Convergence to fundamental value is not the base case for this cohort within a year; partial convergence is.

The business scenarios are set out in the assumptions and priced by the engine. In the base case revenue grows 22.0% in FY2027E with the operating-expense ratio falling as modelled, and the twelve-month value is Rp83 at a 50.0% probability [S0]. The bear case, at 25.0%, subtracts three points of revenue growth and two points of gross margin — the two drivers the mix has already moved against the company — and values the shares at Rp25 [S3][S7]. The bull case, at 25.0%, adds the same three points of growth and two points of margin, and values them at Rp165. The shocks are mirrored by construction, on the same two drivers and the same size; the asymmetry in the result comes from the margin base both scenarios start from, not from the scenario design.

The regime scenarios are a separate dimension and are not the business scenarios. The konglo overlay applies the deck's 35.0% base compression plus the HSC adjustment in its base case, more in the regime bear (which targets Rp108) and none in the regime bull, where the premium re-expands to Rp296 [S13]. The two bear cases compound: a margin disappointment and a further de-rating would land the shares near the regime bear value, not the business bear value.

The regime probabilities (25.0% bear, 50.0% base, 25.0% bull) are the konglo deck's cohort-wide weights, not per-name inputs our tooling can set, and the review is right that this name's flow argues for a heavier bear weight: the stock trades little, the IHSG exit is days away and the MSCI decision falls inside the window [S13][S12]. We tested it rather than assert it. At an even base/bear split the regime target lands between the base and bear regime values, still below the price; making the bear the base regime takes it to the regime bear value. Both are still REDUCE. The choice moves the size of the call, not its direction, and we disclose the test rather than tune the deck to our conclusion.
The risks that matter, with our likelihood and impact:

items: **Growth quality (high likelihood, high impact).** The institution and store segments carry the growth and
the lowest margin; if public-sector and enterprise procurement normalise, revenue growth falls toward the
marketplace rate and the operating leverage in our forecast arrives later [S3][S2].
**Gross-margin mix (high, high).** The margin already fell to 15.6% from 17.6%; another leg
down removes the FY2028E breakeven, which is where most of the value sits [S7].
**Liquidity and funding (high, high).** Net debt peaks at IDR7,720.1bn in FY2029E in
our base, about 3.3 times that year's EBITDA and near the book equity of
the business; if the placement proposed in May is not approved, the gap is debt-funded and interest
compounds the loss years, and if it is approved it can be executed at a discount to market and dilute
minorities without pre-emptive rights [S8][S0].
**Regulatory and index regime (medium, medium).** The concentration-list treatment, the free-float
staircase and the MSCI Standalone decision are dated, cohort-wide events that change who can own the
shares rather than what the business earns [S12][S13].
**Governance and related parties (medium, medium).** Asset sales and capital increases are decided inside
the group; the Halodoc sale to the parent is the template [S9].
**Competition (high, medium).** Larger platforms can outspend Blibli on vouchers and logistics, and the
marketplace line already grows at single digits [S3].
**Macro and currency (medium, low).** Discretionary demand depends on real incomes and the rupiah; Blibli
earns and spends in rupiah, so translation risk is small, but imported electronics carry cost risk [S0].

blocks.text: Signposts that would change the view: two consecutive quarters of double-digit marketplace growth with a stable or rising gross margin; an operating-expense ratio below the base path without a revenue deceleration; a placement executed at or above market with proceeds funding working capital rather than losses; and any evidence that the free float is rising toward the exchange's floor through genuine sell-down rather than issuance [S13].

Blibli is controlled by the Hartono family through the Djarum group. Its largest shareholder is PT Global Investama Andalan, the family's holding company, which is also the counterparty in the Halodoc transaction [S0][S9]. The house konglo registry identifies Djarum (Hartono family) as the controlling group and lists the company on the high-shareholding-concentration register [S13].

The free float is the one input in this report we could not reconcile, and we state the discrepancy rather than assert compliance. The registry records a float of 23.8% against the exchange's floor [S13]; the data pack records insider holdings of 91.2%, which implies an economic float of about one eleventh of the shares — below the lowest tier of the exchange's staircase and inside the lens's window to the first step [S0][S13]. The two numbers use different definitions: the registry measures the shares the exchange treats as free float, the pack measures reported insider holdings, and the pack's own institutional field of 0.8% is consistent with either — it is a small share of even the narrower implied float — so it neither confirms nor contradicts the registry figure. The non-reconciliation rests on that definitional difference, not on an arithmetic inconsistency between the fields [S0][S13]. We hold no annual report, monthly shareholder registry or latest-basis report for this name and could not archive one in this session, so the controller's exact holding and the above-five-percent holders are unverified.

The consequence for the overlay is one-way. If the true float is below the lowest tier, the deck's free-float deadline adjustment adds five points to the compression applied in every regime [S13]. The base regime target falls from Rp173 by several rupiah and the probability-weighted target falls with it; the published target does not include the adjustment because the engine reads the registry figure [S13]. We do not assert that the company is compliant, we do not add the adjustment to a target the engine cannot compute, and we log the registry correction for the Director [S0][S13].

The regime flags we can evidence are specific and dated. The HSC list is a disclosure status and not a finding of wrongdoing, but its consequences are mechanical: HSC shares leave the IHSG, and from 13 November 2026 Blibli is out of that calculation [S12][S13]. The registry records no enforcement action against the company and no bridge event, which we report as absence of evidence rather than as a clean bill [S13]. The free-float staircase is the live deadline: the obligation ratchets up through the decade, which for a controlled company means either controller sell-downs or new shares [S13].

Related-party dealings are the modal risk on this exchange and deserve the plain statement. The company sold a minority preferred stake in Halodoc to its own parent for IDR0.54tn, at a disclosed price, describing the asset as non-core and saying the proceeds were booked into profit — "hasil dari divestasi itu dimasukkan dalam keuntungan perusahaan" [S9]. That is the pattern to expect: portfolio clean-up transacted inside the group, at prices minorities do not negotiate. The registry records no pledge flag on the controlling stake and no enforcement action [S13]; we hold no annual report for this name, so pledges, related-party balances and the auditor's opinion are unverified rather than clean, and that gap is a reason the rating carries no benefit of the doubt.

The board changed at the latest annual meeting: Imron Hendrata was appointed president commissioner and Cyrillus Harinowo independent commissioner [S6]. Kusumo Martanto fronts the results releases for the company [S2][S7], and there is no dividend record to speak of — none has been paid, and the payout is set at zero in our model [S6][S0].

ESG exposures are the ordinary ones for an omnichannel retailer with a logistics arm: packaging and last-mile emissions, labour practices in warehousing and delivery partners, data privacy across four consumer platforms, and the governance of AI-driven merchandising that management is now promoting [S2]. The company's disclosure on these points is narrative rather than quantified in the sources we hold, and we treat it as unproven rather than adverse.

The dated catalysts are the index and regime events, not the results calendar. On 13 November 2026 the HSC shares leave the IHSG calculation, which removes a passive bid that has already been absent in practice [S12]. By the end of June 2027 MSCI decides on Standalone status for Indonesia, a cohort-wide re-rating or de-rating event that Blibli cannot influence [S13]. The FY2026 audited accounts are due by the end of March 2027 and are the first full-year test of the cost base that produced the 2026 improvement [S3]. The same date is the first step of the exchange's free-float staircase, which is why the float question is a dated catalyst and not only a disclosure issue [S13]. The placement proposed to the June 2026 meetings can be approved and executed at any time, and its pricing will tell us how the group intends to fund the remaining loss years [S8].
The KPIs we monitor between updates:

items: **Take rate and gross margin together.** Take rate rose to 9.1%, but gross margin fell to
15.6%; the pair only creates value if the margin stops falling while the take rate rises [S2][S7].
**Operating expense to revenue.** IDR5,895.9bn on IDR31,529.1bn of revenue
in our FY2026E; the whole margin thesis is that this ratio keeps falling without revenue decelerating [S3].
**Marketplace growth against institution growth.** The third-party line at IDR1.20tn grew 9.0% while
institution grew 70.0%; a narrowing gap would be the first evidence of platform, rather than distribution,
growth [S3].
**Cash and net debt.** Net debt of IDR7,720.1bn at the peak in our base, close to book
equity and about 3.3 times that year's EBITDA, and the placement
decision, are the funding signposts [S0][S8].
**Store productivity.** 347 consumer-electronics stores at the end of September 2026 against
265 at the end of 2025; revenue per store, not store count, is what the model needs [S2][S6].
**Free float and HSC status.** The registry says 23.8%, the pack's insider
figure implies far less; an annual report or monthly registry that settles it is the disclosure to watch,
and it would move the konglo overlay, not the fundamentals [S13][S0].

bear.narrative: Discount intensity keeps rising and the institution and physical-store mix keeps diluting gross margin: gross margin gives back two points, revenue growth halves as public-sector procurement normalises, and the operating loss persists past FY2028E while the debt-funded branch raises interest. The shock is the mirror of the bull on the same two drivers.

bull.narrative: Discount intensity normalises: gross profit before discount already grew 20% to Rp 6.11trn and the take rate rose from 8.4% to 9.1% (9.3% in Q3), so a gross margin back to the 17.0-17.6% of the prior-year nine months is the recovery the evidence supports [S2][S3]. The 347 stores mature into positive contribution, the institution business is renewed at better terms and operating profit arrives earlier. The shock is the mirror of the bear on the same two drivers.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-10-22): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S3]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the 9M26 actual (Rp 22.2trn, +46% yoy) plus a Q4 at the third-quarter pace: Q3 revenue grew about +31% and Q1 +67%, so a Q4 at that latest quarterly rate gives FY2026E of about Rp 31.6trn, or +41%, which is what the number now is. The earlier 38% implied a Q4 step-down to +19% that no source supports [S2][S6]. Growth then decelerates toward the measured market: e-Conomy SEA 2026 puts Indonesian e-commerce GMV growth at +16% for 2026 [S10], and Blibli's own quarterly growth already stepped down from +67% (Q1) to +31% (Q3) as the institution segment annualised [S6][S2]. FY2030E +12% is the mature omnichannel rate; long run is terminal growth.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The 9M26 gross margin was 15.6%, down from 17.6%, because the fastest-growing lines are the lowest margin: institution revenue +70% and physical stores +37%, against 3P marketplace revenue +9% [S3][S7]. The margin is therefore held at the 9M26 level and only recovers slowly as the 3P take rate rises (8.4% to 9.1%, 9.3% in Q3 alone) and the new stores mature [S2]; no recovery beyond the mix evidence is assumed.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Operating expense was Rp 4.31trn, down 1% yoy, on revenue +46%: 19.4% of revenue for 9M26 against 26.6% for FY2025 [S3][S6]. The nine-month cash cost base annualises to about Rp 5.75trn, so the forecast is an absolute cost line growing roughly with inflation and the store estate (347 stores at end-September against 265 at end-2025, 15 warehouses), and the ratios below are that same absolute path divided by the revenue build [S2][S6]. The ratio flattens near 11% and the long run holds that level.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The company's own nine-month bridge gives D&A of Rp 217bn: EBITDA of -566 against an operating loss of -783 (and 220 against -1,680 for 9M25), which is about 1.0% of 9M26 revenue of Rp 22,238bn [S3]. The data pack's D&A line, by contrast, is 557 for FY2025A and 449 across the three 2026 quarters — roughly double the charge the reported EBIT-to-EBITDA bridge implies — and the pack's 9M26 EBITDA of about -309 is correspondingly inconsistent with the company's reported -566 [S0][S3]. We model the company basis: 1.0% of revenue, held flat because D&A has been flat in absolute terms (217 in 9M26 against 220 in 9M25) and rises only with the store estate [S3][S2].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capex runs at 1.2% of revenue in the first nine months of 2026 (Rp 272bn) and 1.7% in FY2025A, so 1.5% through the rollout years is the observed rate carried forward while the store estate reached 347 consumer-electronics stores, 60 Ranch Market and 39 Dekoruma units by September 2026 [S0][S2][S6]. From FY2030E capex converges on the depreciation charge and the terminal reinvestment rate: with 4% terminal growth and a 15% return on capital the business must reinvest about a quarter of NOPAT, which on the FY2035E NOPAT of about Rp 2.87trn is Rp 0.78trn, of which the working-capital build at 13.4% of the revenue increment absorbs Rp 0.36trn and capex less D&A the remaining Rp 0.42trn. At D&A of 1.0% of revenue that is capex at about 1.6% of revenue, and terminal FCFF stays below NOPAT; the earlier 3.1% was tied to a D&A ratio (2.6%) the company does not report [S3].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The LTM balance sheet carries operating working capital of Rp 3.92trn on LTM revenue of Rp 29.36trn, 13.4%, as inventory and receivables grew with the 1P and institution businesses [S0][S3].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Statutory Indonesian corporate rate of 22% on forecast profits; the company pays almost nothing today because it is loss-making, so the forecast applies the statutory rate to a positive EBIT path and assumes the accumulated tax losses absorb the transition years. The pack's 10% history is an artefact of tax on a negative pre-tax result [S0].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest expense of Rp 238bn on opening debt of Rp 2.22trn, 10.7%, close to the rupiah risk-free rate plus the corporate spread in the macro deck; set at 10.5% [S0].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of Rp 67bn on opening cash of Rp 2.45trn, 2.7%; held at the pack yield [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The residual funding gap is met with debt at the pace already observed: gross debt rose from Rp 3.61trn to Rp 4.20trn in the first nine months of 2026 (+Rp 0.59trn) [S0]. On the reported D&A basis (1.0% of revenue, not the pack's 2.6%) the free-cash outflow is larger than a pack-based model shows, so the borrowing path is sized to keep the cash balance above Rp 0.5trn until free cash flow turns positive: Rp 0.9trn in FY2026E, rising to Rp 2.0trn in FY2027E and Rp 1.9trn in FY2028E, then falling as operating cash flow improves. Gross debt peaks near Rp 9.6trn and interest expense near Rp 1.0trn a year, which is the solvency question the report addresses. The 9.5bn-share PMTHMETD/MESOP is a proposal put to the 4 June 2026 meetings, not an approved or priced issue in our sources; it has no disclosed price, no use of proceeds and no result, and the engine has no line for issue proceeds [S8]. We therefore keep the debt-funded branch as the base and treat the placement branch in the report: executed at the last price it would raise roughly Rp 2.2trn and be accretive per share (issue price above fundamental value), executed at a discount it would transfer value to the subscriber [S8].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: No recurring other non-operating line is forecast: the last material one, the Halodoc divestment gain, was a one-off [S9].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interest is small (Rp 186bn on the balance sheet) and loss-making subsidiaries absorb a minor share; held at the pack average [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. Blibli has never paid a dividend, is loss-making and needs the cash to fund working capital and the store rollout; the 2025 AGM approved no distribution [S6][S0].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: +1% a year: the share count rose from 135.8bn to 137.2bn in the first nine months of 2026 through the employee scheme [S0]. A further 9.5bn shares (4.5bn MESOP plus 5bn of new capital without pre-emptive rights) was proposed to the 4 June 2026 shareholder meetings; we do not add it to the share count because no approval, price or execution is in our sources, and adding the shares without the proceeds would be a one-sided haircut [S8].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set equal to the model's own long-run revenue growth (4%) rather than the 5% cap. A terminal that capitalises cash flows growing faster than revenue forever is internally inconsistent, and at 5% the terminal value outgrew the revenue line from FY2031E onward. Indonesian long-run nominal GDP growth is real growth of 5.3% plus inflation near 3.3% in the macro deck, so 4% sits well inside the economy and inside the house 5% cap; the value effect of the 1pp cut is disclosed in the valuation section.

challenges.challenge: Section 6 states the free float is 23.81% and the company is compliant today with the raised floor, while the same paragraph reports insider holdings of 91.2% from the data pack. Both cannot hold: heldPercentInsiders is 91.192% in fund record, implying an 8.81% float, below the 12.5% tier with the 12.5% step due 31 Mar 2027, inside the lens's 18-month window. The controller's stake required by the konglo card is never given, and S13 does not contain 23.81% (it is in coverage/universe/idxic_snapshot.csv, and cov_konglo cites deck source S25).
challenges.answer: FATAL accepted as a disclosure failure: [S13] registry says 23.8% and [S0] pack says 91.2% insiders; the definitions cannot be reconciled from the sources we hold, so the governance section states both, the implied ~8.8% economic float, the missing annual report/LBRE, and that the overlay's free-float deadline adjustment would lower the base regime and final target; compliance is no longer asserted and the registry correction is logged for the Director.

challenges.challenge: The EV/Sales leg carries 40% of value (Rp78 vs DCF Rp118) on a 0.426x 'peer median' whose four contributors are EMTK (media), MCAS (digital payments/telco), NFCX (IT services) and WIFI (fiber/tower, 2.72x); the only two Indonesian marketplace comparables, BUKA and GOTO, have no EV/Sales in the pack and are excluded. The report explains the -34.4% divergence as 'platforms whose revenue is high-margin take rate', which misdescribes the actual set, and cites the multiple to S0 (Yahoo), which cannot contain peer multiples.
challenges.answer: Accepted: EV/sales weight cut to 20% with DCF at 80%; the peer table is shown and the four contributors named, BUKA and GOTO are excluded because their packs carry no EV/sales (net cash, take-rate revenue), the non-marketplace median mismatch is stated, and the zero-weight case (blend = DCF) is disclosed; the 40% weight and the misdescription are gone [S0][S3].

challenges.challenge: COE 14.68% and WACC 13.83% sit above the house 11-13% IDR band. The justification, that the beta is an industry default rather than a regression and that FCF is negative through FY2028E, raises the discount rate for losses the cash flows already contain. The model's own sensitivity gives DCF Rp139 at 12.83% WACC (roughly Rp155 near band-mid), at which the blend, the 12-month fundamental and the konglo target all reach or clear Rp232, flipping the rating to HOLD/NEUTRAL. Section 4 never says the call depends on this input.
challenges.answer: Accepted: beta_unlevered is a 1.0 company parameter, giving COE 13.2% and WACC 12.5% inside the house band; section 4 explains that country and small-float risks sit in the CRP and the liquidity discount, that the old rate double-counted the loss years, and that across the band the DCF runs roughly 86 to 99 with the rating REDUCE at either edge [S0].

challenges.challenge: S8 is dated 15 May 2026 and says the 9.5bn-share PMTHMETD/MESOP 'akan dimintakan persetujuan' at the 4 June 2026 RUPST/RUPSLB; it does not report the outcome. The report states four times that the placement 'was approved in June 2026' citing S8 (summary, section 3, section 4, section 5, section 7) on the funding route and the dilution catalyst. The quote does not say what the report claims.
challenges.answer: Accepted: S8 is a pre-approval report of the 15 May 2026 plan; every reference now says the placement was proposed to the 4 June 2026 meetings and is not approved or priced, section 3 prices both branches, and the base keeps the debt-funded path until approval and terms exist [S8][S0].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue 30,791 equals 9M actual 22,238 plus Q4E 8,553, i.e. Q4 +19.4% yoy against +46% for 9M and about +31% in 3Q (Q1 +67%). The stated basis, 'Q4 at the 9M26 exit pace', reproduces about 31.6trn (+41%), not 30.8trn: number and basis disagree, and the lower base propagates into every later year. On a near-fixed opex base this is about Rp0.7trn of FY2026E EBITDA.
challenges.answer: Accepted: FY2026E revenue is rebuilt as the 9M actual plus a Q4 at the Q3 pace, 31,529bn or +41%, and basis, section 3 and the DCF now agree; the unsourced Q4 step-down to +19% is removed and later years carry the higher base [S2][S6].

challenges.challenge: Revenue grows 4.0% a year from FY2031E (revenue_growth lt 0.04) but terminal value capitalises FY2035E FCFF at 5.0%, so FCFF outgrows revenue forever. In FY2035E capex is 1,024 (1.5% of revenue) against D&A 1,775 and delta-NWC 352, so FCFF 3,062 exceeds NOPAT 2,663: the terminal assumes a perpetually shrinking asset base. Terminal value is 61.6% of EV.
challenges.answer: Accepted: terminal growth is cut to 4% to match the long-run revenue fade and capex rises from 1.5% to 3.1% of revenue from FY2031E so terminal reinvestment is g/ROIC at a 15% return; FY2035E FCFF is now 2,164 against NOPAT above 2,800, so FCFF no longer exceeds NOPAT [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: The multiple-survival sentence says the terminal EBITDA multiple is 'no higher than the entry multiple on gross profit'. Terminal EV/EBITDA is 36,402/5,189 = 7.0x; entry EV/gross profit is 18,092/4,803 = 3.8x. 7.0x is nearly double 3.8x and the two are not comparable metrics, so the test as written is false and does not answer the card's question about what a rational buyer would pay.
challenges.answer: Accepted: the false 7.0x against 3.8x comparison is replaced; the terminal block on FY2035E EBITDA is a mid-single-digit multiple against the 21.0x market EV/EBITDA on FY2028E EBITDA, and on gross profit the terminal multiple is close to the DCF entry multiple on FY2026E gross profit for a base more than twice the size [S0].

challenges.challenge: The placement is the stated funding route but the model neither adds the 9.5bn shares (6.9% of 137.2bn) nor the proceeds: share_change is +1%/yr and the gap is met with Rp600bn/yr of new debt. At 6.9% dilution the DCF and EV/Sales per-share values and the konglo target fall about 6.5% (204 to about 191); without the placement net debt peaks higher and interest compounds the loss years. Section 5 names the dilution but no number reaches the valuation.
challenges.answer: Rebutted in part with evidence: the engine has no equity-proceeds line, so adding 9.5bn shares without roughly Rp2.2trn of cash would be a one-sided haircut, and [S8] shows no approval, price or use of proceeds; section 3 now sizes the dilution at about one new share in fourteen and prices both branches in prose, with the base debt-funded until terms exist [S8][S0].

challenges.challenge: The report never uses its strongest bull evidence: gross profit before discount rose 20% to Rp6.11trn (F12) and the take rate rose from 8.4% to 9.1% (9.3% in 3Q, F11). Gross margin fell to 15.6% only because discounts widened, yet the base pins margin at 15.6-16.5%, 1.1pp below the 17.6% of 9M25, and neither the bull scenario nor section 5 lets discount intensity normalise. At 17.0% in FY2030E, EBITDA is about Rp0.8trn higher and the DCF about Rp15/share higher.
challenges.answer: Accepted: GPBD growth (F40) and the 8.4% to 9.1% take rate are now in section 1 and in the bull case, and the bull adds two points of gross margin against the bear's two-point cut, so normalisation toward the 17.0-17.6% prior-year range is priced and mirrored [S3][S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 argues that no buyer exists and the placement mandate runs the other way, which is the case for faster premium compression, yet the overlay keeps deck-default 50/25/25 probabilities and closes only 35% of the log gap. On the report's own logic the 75% bear regime deserves more weight: bear-as-base gives 136 (minus 41%), a 50/50 base/bear mix gives 189 (minus 18%). The probabilities are not argued for this name and the prose and parameters pull in opposite directions.
challenges.answer: Accepted as an argument, not a parameter change: the deck's 25/50/25 regime weights are cohort-wide and not per-name settable; section 5 argues them with ADTV, the IHSG exit and the MSCI date and shows that an even base/bear split leaves the target between the base and bear regime values and still REDUCE [S13][S12].

challenges.challenge: The summary asserts that 'the Djarum group has repeatedly recapitalised this business rather than lever it' with no citation, and neither section 1 nor section 4 prices the group option: a controlled vehicle with a placement mandate and a related-party asset-sale precedent can fund or inject assets. No recapitalisation history, size or source appears, so the affirmational half of the governance read is unverifiable while the risk half is quantified.
challenges.answer: Accepted: the uncited recapitalisation claim is replaced by the sourced share-count history, 118,493m in FY2022A to 135,843m in FY2025A and 137,201m at 9M26, with no dividend paid, so equity-funded expansion is evidenced rather than asserted; the group option is not added as a bridge because no injection is sourced [S0][S6].

challenges.challenge: Rendered section 4 prints 'the market capitalisation is IDR31,834,804,679.85tn', a 1e3 unit error (31,834.8bn = Rp31.8tn); 'from an enterprise value of IDR18,092.1bn after net debt, minorities and the investment portfolio' describes EV 18,092, which is before the bridge, when equity is 16,240; section 3 labels FY2025A FCFF (-3,800.9) as 'operating cash flow'; and section 4's 'blended value today is Rp102' rolled forward and discounted would give 105.3, not the Rp109 produced by the probability-weighted 105.16.
challenges.answer: Accepted: market cap now uses the bn scaling (IDR31,834.8bn), the EV sentence separates the DCF enterprise value from the equity bridge, FY2025A FCFF is labelled free cash flow rather than operating cash flow, and the value chain is stated as v0 87 to tp_base 99 to weighted 105 to fundamental 95 after the liquidity discount [S0].

challenges.challenge: Several specifics are uncited or overstate their source: Blibli's address in Kudus, Central Java citing S2 and S9 (neither source mentions Kudus); the Halodoc sale 'booked as a gain' citing S9 (S9 reports Rp538.48bn proceeds and a non-core rationale, not a gain); 'no going-concern opinion, no delinquency, no auditor qualification' are uncited negative assertions; and 'moved several strategic categories from the marketplace to first-party' overstates S2, which says 1P shifted focus to higher-margin products.
challenges.answer: Accepted: Kudus and the parent are cited to the data pack [S0], the Halodoc gain is supported by the S9 quote on proceeds booked into profit, the going-concern, delinquency and audit assertions are removed or recast as absence of evidence, the CFO name is dropped, and the first-party wording now follows S2 on higher-margin focus [S0][S9][S2].

missing_bull_case.note: Take-rate and GBPD upside (GBPD +20% to Rp6.11trn, take rate 8.4 to 9.1%, 9.3% in 3Q) and Djarum group support are noted but never priced; the base pins gross margin at the 9M trough and no scenario lets discount intensity normalise.

missing_bear_case.note: The 9.5bn-share (6.9%) placement without pre-emptive rights is disclosed but neither modelled nor valued, and the no-placement branch (Rp600bn/yr new debt, higher interest) is not quantified; public-sector dependence of the institution segment is named, not sized.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E revenue 30,791 implies Q4 8,553, +19.4% yoy against +46% for 9M and about +31% in 3Q, while the stated basis ('Q4 at the 9M26 exit pace') reproduces about 31.6trn (+41%). Terminal g 5% also exceeds the model's own 4.0% revenue fade from FY2031E.

evidence_and_citations.note: S8 (15 May 2026) reports a placement plan due for approval on 4 June 2026, not an approved placement; the 23.81% float is cited to S13 but lives in the IDX-IC snapshot and conflicts with the pack's 91.19% insider figure; the peer median multiple is cited to S0 (Yahoo), which cannot contain it.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF mechanics are sound (Q4-2026 stub factor 0.2519, bridge at 30 Sep 2026, TV 61.6% of EV). But WACC 13.8% is above the 11-13% house band on an industry-default beta, EV/Sales carries 40% on a multiple the report itself calls inapplicable, and the multiple-survival sentence compares 7.0x terminal EV/EBITDA with 3.8x entry EV/gross profit.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is disciplined and the call is not one heroic input, but section 4's own reasoning (no buyer, placement mandate, small float) argues for faster premium compression than the 35% base it keeps; the 50/25/25 regime probabilities are deck defaults not argued for this name, so text and parameters lean opposite ways.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Uses the right GMV deck (e-Conomy 16%, USD85bn e-commerce of USD119bn) and the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP and 3.28% CPI, but never reflects the macro desk's CAUTIOUS regime and AVOID tilt on ID consumer discretionary, and the EV/Sales peer set is not the sector's internet cohort.

conservatism_audit.note: Only one unsourced drift below the last actual: the Q4-26 revenue step-down; gross margin, opex, tax and royalty-type rates are anchored or sourced. Mirrored shocks are symmetric (+/-3pp growth, +/-1.5pp margin, 50/25/25). But 40% weight on a self-declared inapplicable multiple plus a band-breaching WACC is a stack that moves the rating from REDUCE to HOLD.

calibration.note: Model is fresh with no blocking flags; both BLOCK flags are justified by the 9M26 actuals (EBITDA loss -61%, opex 19.4% of revenue vs 26.6%) and tie to F6/F7. FY2026E EBITDA margin -0.8% vs -6.4% is the observed nine-month run-rate, not a forecast uplift.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. Verified: FY2026E = 9M22,238 + Q4 9,291 at the Q3 pace (+30.5%), +41%; gross margin 15.6%, opex 18.7%, D&A 1.0% (217bn 9M26 bridge); DCF EV 11,730.8 - net debt 2,832.2 - minorities 185.9 + associates 1,166.2 = equity 9,879.0 / 137.2bn = Rp72.0; EV/Sales 0.426x LTM 29,359.8 = Rp77.7; blend 73, base 83, weighted 89 x 0.9 = fundamental 80.13; konglo premium 232/70.78 = 3.278, compress base 0.30 + HSC 0.05 = 0.35, premium kept 2.341 x 80.13 = Rp187.6, rounded 188. The lens is on the right base (fundamental 12-month value, pre-lens) and REDUCE survives a heavier bear (a 50/50 base/bear regime is further below price). Konglo name read as a group: Djarum, HSC, IHSG exit 13 Nov, MSCI Jun-2027; no sibling marked at market. Free-float discrepancy (registry 23.81% vs pack insiders 91.19% implying about 8.8%) is disclosed, not asserted, and logged for the Director; the ff-deadline adjustment would cut the target to about 180, still REDUCE. Carried to v2 and named: (Q10) s4 and s5 still call 0.35 the deck base compression plus the HSC adjustment when the deck is 0.30 and HSC adds 0.05 - the engine applies 0.35 once (correct) but the prose reads as 0.40; (Q11) s3 says the prior-year D&A arithmetic gives the same answer but 9M25 EBITDA -1.46trn vs EBIT -1.68trn = Rp220bn on revenue 15,239 = 1.44%, not 1.0% (the 1.0% model basis is the conservative one); (Q12) s2 prints 119bn/85bn/446bn without USD. Q14, Q16 and Q17 stand as NOTE-only to v2. None changes the rating or target.

bias.note: Base case is anchored on the last actual, not on caution: FY2026E revenue is the 9M26 actual of IDR22,238bn plus a Q4 at the Q3 pace (IDR31,529bn, +41.0%) [S2]; gross margin is held at the 15.6% print to FY2030E and recovers only to 16.5%; opex is flat in real terms with the ratio falling to 11.2% on the measured 9M26 leverage (19.4% of revenue, 6.4% of TPV) [S3][S6]; capex 1.5-1.6% sits inside the observed 1.2-1.7% [S0]; terminal g 4% equals the long-run revenue growth and the terminal reinvestment is 27% of FY2035E NOPAT at ~15% ROIC [S0]. COE 13.2% / WACC 12.5% are inside the 11-13% IDR band [S0]. Scenarios are mirrored on the same two drivers (growth +/-3pp, margin +/-2pp) at 50/25/25; the wide value spread (Rp25 vs Rp165) is operating leverage at breakeven, not an asymmetric shock. The only departure from the 9M run-rate is FY2026E EBITDA at -2.1% against the reported -2.5%, which is disclosed and follows from Q4 revenue on a flat cost base [S3]. No unsourced conservatism or optimism found that moves the rating.

findings.finding: Q3 is only half fixed. Section 5 still reads 'the konglo overlay applies the deck's 35.0% base compression plus the HSC adjustment in its base case', and section 4 now calls 35.0% 'the deck's 35.0% base compression'. The deck's compress_base is 0.30 [konglo deck]; the engine's 0.35 is that 0.30 plus the HSC +0.05, so 'plus the HSC adjustment' tells a reader the base closure is 40% when the engine applies 35%. The targets (173/108/296) and the Rp188 target are computed correctly, so this is prose, not valuation.

Section 3 says the D&A bridge 'gives D&A of 1.0% of revenue, and the same arithmetic on the prior-year comparative gives the same answer [S3]'. It does not: 9M25 EBITDA of -1.46trn against an operating loss of -1.68trn gives Rp220bn on 9M25 revenue of Rp15,239bn, or 1.44%, not 1.0%. The charge is flat in absolute terms (217 vs 220), which is what fund record correctly says, but the ratio fell with revenue. This is the corroboration for the da_pct restatement that carried the Q1 BLOCK, so it has to be exact.

Section 2 prints three USD figures with no currency: 'the digital economy reached 119bn of gross merchandise value in 2026', 'e-commerce was 85bn' and '446bn or more by 2035'. The placeholders {{fact.F24|num0}}, {{fact.F23|num0}} and {{fact.F38|num0}} drop the USD unit the facts carry [S10], so the numbers read as rupiah billions, a 1e4 unit defect in the market-size paragraph.

The accepted answer to C6 still says capex 'rises from 1.5% to 3.1% of revenue from FY2031E'; the model line is 1.6% (1,118.6 / 69,911.1) and the terminal block rests on total reinvestment of about 27% of FY2035E NOPAT, which is what supports 4% growth at ~15% ROIC. The judge raised the same point. No change to the model or the report is needed.

The reverse DCF still does not bracket Rp232, and section 4 asserts the price 'requires a terminal operating margin above what the mix supports' without the number. The judge flagged it again. Neither the target nor the rating depends on it.

The EV/sales leg (20% weight) reproduces at 0.426x from EMTK 0.247, MCAS 0.304, NFCX 0.549 and WIFI 2.723, and the target holds at Rp188. Sibling INTERNET_PLATFORMS writes are running concurrently, so a later shift in this median is a peer-state artefact to re-check at sign-off, not a finding on BELI.

The FY2026E equity roll-forward lands at IDR7,953.8bn against the reported 30-Sep-2026 equity of IDR8,748.6bn, a ~9% gap because the model starts from the pack's FY2025A equity and has no line for the 1.4bn MESOP shares issued (the C8 engine limitation). The valuation bridge is unaffected (FCFF carries no equity), but the 'close to book equity' leverage sentence and the ROE/PBV sit on a low base.

The compounder card's pre-profit platform gate is met only by inference: section 1 gives GPBD (+20% to Rp6.11trn) and the 9.1% take rate but never states the contribution line after discounts, which is 9M26 gross profit of Rp3.46trn against cash operating expense of about Rp4.09trn. The gate wants positive unit economics today with no terminal rescue; the DCF's terminal value is 74% of EV.
